prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a staircase scene where the camera wearer's left hand and a sloping metal handrail in the foreground are brightest and within arm's reach (roughly 0.2–0.5 m away), while the marble steps behind them recede from about 0.8 m to 2.0 m. In frames 1–4, the wearer's right hand and a vertical spirit level sit just below the handrail at around 0.4–0.6 m, while a second person's arm is partially visible at the lower-left edge about 1.0–1.5 m away, before the camera turns left and downward in frame 5 to reveal that second person standing on the lower steps about 1.5–2.5 m below and in front of the wearer. In frame 5, this second person faces toward the staircase and looks upward toward the handrail area rather than directly at the camera wearer, with his left hand touching the lower rail (about 1.2 m from the wearer) and a handheld power tool in his right hand within his own reach; meanwhile, the wearer's own shoulder/arm enters the bottom-right foreground at under 0.3 m, partially occluding the handrail. Compared to the RGB strip, the depth map makes the continuous 3D depth ordering of the receding steps, vertical balusters, and foreground limbs immediately clear despite specular reflections on the chrome rail and pale marble. However, the map looks unreliable along the bottom-right floor and doorway area in frames 1–4 and the stairwell gap in frame 5, which collapse into uniform black voids, and it slightly flattens the second person's torso and grinder into a single mid-grey depth plane in frame 5.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates only "person" regions against a black background, capturing the camera wearer's foreground left arm and C-shaped hand gripping the rail (0.3–0.5 m away) across frames 1–4 and the standing man on the lower steps (about 1.5–2.0 m away, below and to the left) in frame 5. In frame 1, it also detects a small brown mask for the wearer's partially occluded right hand at the bottom center (around 0.5 m away), and in frames 2–4 it includes parts of the second worker's distant arm at the far left edge (1.0–1.5 m away). Across frames 1–4 the foreground left hand stays in a steady position while the handrail it wraps around forms a sharp concave cutout in the mask, and in frame 5 the camera pans left to show the second person's full silhouette facing up the stairs with his left arm extended to the rail. While the map cleanly separates the second worker's body silhouette from the dimly lit stairwell in frame 5, it fails to segment any non-person objects within reach—such as the handrail, spirit level, stairs, or angle grinder—and completely misses the wearer's foreground arm at the bottom right of frame 5. It is also unreliable in frames 2–4, where it merges the distant worker's arm with the wearer's foreground arm into a single mask (frames 2 and 4) or splits the wearer's own hand and sleeve into two separate "person" instances (frame 3).
descriptions.pose: The pose map tracks 2D skeletal keypoints, showing only the camera wearer's close-up left hand (0.3–0.5 m away) in frames 1, 3, and 4, and the second person's full body skeleton standing below on the stairs (1.5–2.0 m away) in frame 5. In frames 3 and 4, the magenta hand skeletons clearly trace the thumb and four fingers wrapping around the cylindrical handrail within arm's reach, whereas frame 5 shows the second person's yellow torso, legs, both arms, and facial keypoints oriented toward the right/upstairs and looking toward the handrail rather than at the camera wearer. The distance between the wearer's foreground hand in frames 1–4 and the second person's position down the stairs in frame 5 is roughly 1.0–1.5 m, with the second person's left wrist reaching up to contact the lower rail and his right wrist hanging down by the grinder. In frame 5, the pose map reveals the full-body joint articulations and head orientation of the man in the shadowed stairwell more explicitly than the RGB image alone. However, the map is highly unreliable on egocentric close-ups: it completely misses all keypoints in frame 2, misses the wearer's right hand and the partially visible background person in frames 1–4, misses the wearer's foreground arm and the man's magenta hand skeletons in frame 5, and hallucinates a tiny, crushed yellow body torso with facial dots inside the wearer's close-up wrist and hand in frames 1, 3, and 4.
